site.title: PlacementScope
site.purpose: Placements at IIT Guwahati run on rumours, forwards and half-true stories. This guide is built from real interviews with seniors who were placed or went on to further studies.
site.event: Sahyog'26 · Students' Welfare Board × Academic Initiatives Club, IIT Guwahati
site.disclaimer: Everything here comes from individual senior experiences. Cutoffs, processes and pay change every year, so check the details with the placement cell before you rely on them.

domains.name: Civil Core
domains.summary: GATE-level fundamentals, form-driven shortlisting and a decisive HR round with a psychologist on the panel.

paragraphs: This section collects placement experience and practical guidance from recent seniors who went through Civil Engineering core campus recruitment.
Core technical rounds and online screening tests closely follow the pattern and weightage of GATE and IES (Engineering Services Examination), so GATE-level preparation is the benchmark.
keyPoints: Prepare core subjects to GATE standard.
Be ready to defend every line of Forms A, B and C.
The HR round plays a decisive role in final selection.

timeline.detail: Structured company CV forms submitted via Google Forms over a 7–10 day window.
Based on CPI and student category. Interview invitations arrive within 1–2 days.
Some companies (e.g. Spectrum Techno Consultant) run an online test open to most shortlisted candidates (14 of 17 in one case). Questions resemble 1-mark GATE questions.
Early-morning pre-placement presentation, then mandatory document verification (Class 10 & 12 marksheets, category certificates).
15–30 minutes with a panel of 6–7 interviewers covering fundamentals and core sub-disciplines.
Candidates who clear the technical round fill Form C immediately.
30–40 minutes; typically a professional psychologist and two HR representatives. The process usually runs until about 3:00 PM.

general: Shortlisting considers CPI and student category.
Category certificates and Class 10 & 12 marksheets are verified on drive day.

roadmap.title: Start a GATE / IES foundation
actions: Begin preparing for IES, or at least GATE, from the first year.
roadmap.outcome: An early base leaves room to handle placement stress alongside college life.

roadmap.title: Build core subjects to GATE standard
actions: Cover Strength of Materials, Structural Analysis, Geotechnical, Transportation and Steel Structures.
Practise 1-mark GATE-style questions for online tests.
roadmap.outcome: Technical rounds and online tests mirror GATE/IES pattern and weightage.

roadmap.title: Prepare your forms
actions: Fill Forms A and B carefully during the 7–10 day window.
Prepare people-management, leadership and crisis-resolution stories for Form C.
roadmap.outcome: Every claim on your forms can survive situational follow-up questions.

roadmap.title: Drive day
actions: Carry Class 10 & 12 marksheets and category certificates.
Stay calm through a long day that runs to about 3 PM.
roadmap.outcome: Steady, confident answers across technical and HR panels.

practical.title: Leadership and project stories
practical.detail: Form C asks about a major achievement, a time outside your comfort zone, or a key group project. Panels check whether your stated leadership and co-curricular experience is genuine.

advice.quote: Prepare standard Civil subjects up to GATE standard; most technical rounds and online tests mirror GATE and IES.

domains.name: Product Management
domains.summary: CPI-gated online tests, guesstimates, product design and RCA, then a live case round on Day 1.

paragraphs: This section is based on a recent senior's first-hand experience of Product Management campus recruitment.
Product profiles on campus span management, strategy and analytics, and the actual work depends heavily on the employer's industry.
keyPoints: Some product recruiters (e.g. Media.net) skip resume shortlisting and use a strict 7.5+ CPI cutoff for the online test.
Club work from the first year builds product, analytics and consulting foundations.
Communication and public speaking show confidence in front of panels.

timeline.detail: Eligibility verified; no resume shortlist, so access to the online test depends on the 7.5+ CPI cutoff.
Guesstimates, product design, RCA and case-study style problems.

timeline.when: About 2 weeks after the online test
timeline.detail: More than 50 candidates on the combined shortlist and waitlist; waitlisted candidates can move into active interviews.
Projects, past internships, guesstimates, product design and root-cause analysis. Only 20–30% advance.
Deep project discussion plus a live business case study.

general: CPI ≥ 7.5 to sit for the online assessment (Media.net).
No initial resume shortlisting for that process.

skills.name: Guesstimates
skills.detail: Structured logic, stated assumptions and sanity checks, communicated step by step.

skills.name: Product design
skills.detail: Designing for user needs in scenario questions.

skills.name: Root-cause analysis (RCA)
skills.detail: Tested in the online assessment and Round 1.

skills.name: Project depth
skills.detail: Explain design decisions, real-world utility and your own contribution.

skills.name: Communication & public speaking
skills.detail: Leading teams and presenting to audiences of up to 100 people builds visible confidence.

roadmap.title: Join the right clubs early
actions: Join and actively contribute to the Consulting and Analytics Club from the 1st year.
roadmap.outcome: Foundations in product management, analytics and consulting frameworks.

roadmap.title: Build communication and leadership
actions: Take roles where you guide teams and present to large audiences.
roadmap.outcome: Visible confidence in front of panels.

roadmap.title: Keep your CPI above 7.5
actions: Protect your CPI; some product tests are gated purely on it.
roadmap.outcome: You get to sit the online assessment at all.

roadmap.title: PPT and online assessment
actions: Attend PPTs in the first week of November.
Practise guesstimates, product design, RCA and case studies for the test about 10 days later.
roadmap.outcome: A place on the Day 1 shortlist.

roadmap.title: Day 1 interviews
actions: Know every project on your resume in depth, including design decisions and your own contribution.
Think out loud with clear assumptions and sanity checks.
roadmap.outcome: Clearing Round 1 (20–30% do) and the live case in Round 2.

practical.detail: Active contribution from the 1st year builds product, analytics and consulting foundations.

practical.title: Projects that hold up to probing
practical.detail: In one Round 2, the interviewer singled out a project on an AI agentic workflow and asked about design decisions, real-world use and individual contribution.

practical.detail: Guiding teams and presenting to audiences of up to 100 people.

myths.myth: A strong resume is what gets you into the product test.
myths.reality: Some recruiters (e.g. Media.net) skip resume shortlisting entirely and admit candidates to the online test on a strict 7.5+ CPI cutoff.

myths.myth: Every PM role is classic consumer product management.
myths.reality: Work varies by industry. At an ad-tech company like Media.net, it centres on advertising algorithms, platform mechanics and publisher tools.

myths.myth: Making the shortlist means you are nearly through.
myths.reality: Over 50 candidates can be on the shortlist and waitlist, and only 20–30% of Round 1 candidates reach Round 2.
